title: Why a Bangalore martech SaaS killed its SDR team and doubled pipeline with inbound content
content: SITUATION: A Bangalore martech SaaS (campaign-attribution tool, ACV ₹18K/month) burned ₹11L/month on a 4-person SDR team cold-emailing and dialling 6,000 prospects/month. Reply rate sat at 1.8%, 22 demos booked/month, but only 3 closed. Loading the full motion, blended CAC was ₹3.6L against an LTV of ₹2.4L — the unit economics were underwater, and payback ran past 18 months versus the board's sub-9-month line. The founder wanted to add 2 more SDRs. ACTION: I said cut, don't add. We redirected ₹6L/month into programmatic SEO plus founder-led LinkedIn: 40 bottom-funnel comparison pages ('vs CleverTap', 'vs WebEngage'), 3 founder posts/week built on real attribution failures, and YouTube teardowns of live dashboards. We kept 1 SDR to chase inbound MQLs only, and moved follow-up from email to WhatsApp. OUTCOME: Within 5 months organic drove 31 demos/month at near-zero marginal cost, LinkedIn added 14 inbound demos/month, and blended CAC fell to ₹84K. Inbound leads arrived problem-aware, so close rate rose to 19%. Pipeline doubled from ₹70L to ₹1.4Cr. WhatsApp follow-ups lifted demo-show rate from 51% to 78%.
lesson: Below ~₹25K/month ACV, outbound SDR economics rarely survive Indian payback math: every month cold outreach resets to zero, while comparison-keyword SEO and founder proof content compound into a free demo engine. Kill the motion that resets before scaling the one that compounds — and for show-rate, WhatsApp beats email every time in India.
